title: Number of Valid Words in a Sentence
summary: A sentence is composed of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, punctuation, and spaces.
statement: A sentence is composed of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, punctuation, and spaces. A valid word must contain only lowercase letters, hyphens, and/or punctuation, with at most one hyphen surrounded by letters and at most one punctuation mark at the end. Examples of valid words are 'a-b.', 'afad', 'ba-c', 'a!', and '!'. Given a sentence, count the number of valid words.
constraints: Tokens are separated by spaces and may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and !., punctuation.
A valid token has no digit, at most one hyphen surrounded by lowercase letters, and at most one punctuation mark only at its end.
Return the number of valid tokens.
hints: Token validity is a small grammar over lowercase runs, one optional internal hyphen, and one optional final punctuation mark.
Split on whitespace and match each whole token against that grammar, also allowing a punctuation-only token.
Anchors require the entire token to match; the grouped optional pieces enforce every count and position rule directly.
editorial: Anchors require the entire token to match; the grouped optional pieces enforce every count and position rule directly.
